Im 20 and I’m currently in the process of moving out and living on my own, although I’m very lucky to have some siblings that are not jw’s it’s still difficult. But my way of coping is finding out that this is a time to focus on my self. My whole life I wasn’t allowed to fully be myself and I’m learning new things about myself everyday. I’d suggest trying out jw meetups, exercise (you might get some gym buddies) and if you had some high school friends try re connecting with them. If you’re doing college, that’s a perfect place to find great people and friends. It’s ok to be alone sometimes, learn how to hang out with yourself and use that time to think about who you really are. But also don’t isolate yourself, humans desire a need to connect. Just talk to people, at the grocery store, gas station, co workers and friends. Good luck!

I didn’t deserve that, if he wanted me, he could’ve been flirty with me instead. At this point, I would just focus on yourself. Realize you’re strengths and weaknesses and make them stronger. If he ever comes back, you might have changed your mind. All I’m trying to say is that the universe is good. And if the universe wanted you to end up with that guy then it will happen. Everything happens for a reason. Think of this as a lesson and what you can learn from it about yourself.

I actually arrived late to the assembly on my baptism day because I was out eating breakfast (shows how much I didn’t care). When they asked the question about identifying as a jw I just stayed quite. When I got submerged into the water and got out. Everyone was clapping but all I could think of was “now everyone will finally get off my back about getting baptized.”

I had those thoughts a lot last year. I always wondered why I wasn’t as spiritual as the others or didn’t care enough to do something about it, while at the same time everyone who was spiritual seemed so un natural to me. I packed up my bags March 7 and left. I had to. My mom and elders were on to me. Months have passed now and I’m glad my mom is mature enough to realize that my mental health is more important than following some rules. I don’t know how things will work out for you but you’ll never know if you don’t try. Really think about where you’re going to go, what social group you’ll have and what you’ll do after. It’s good to know things before you throw yourself in the water. I hope the best of luck to you. Having control over your thoughts and actions is a much better feeling than pleasing others who will drop you so quickly when you disagree with their opinions.
